newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed in light trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds overcame early morning weakness to close mixed in quiet trading on Tuesday as investors continued to cover short positions in the market, dealers said.
Analysts said economic data showing moderate inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy failed to sway bond markets strongly in either direction.

The U.S. Department of Commerce reported June retail sales rose 0.5 percent compared to a downwardly revised 0.3 percent decline in May. Excluding the key automobile component, retail sales rose 0.3 percent.
A Reuters survey had forecast a 0.2 percent rise in sales and a 0.5 percent increase minus the automobile component.

"We're basically following the U.S. (treasuries) with some slight weakness, but that is of no great significance," said Jim Webber, vice-president and director of fixed-income research with Toronto Dominion Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.08 to C$118.57 to yield 6.572 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond climbed 3/32 to yield 6.55 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to two basis points from a spread of three basis points at the close on Monday.
A weaker Canadian dollar also took some of the luster off the Canadian bond market.
The dollar closed at C$1.3703 (US$0.7297) on Tuesday after opening at C$1.3671 (US$0.7314).
"There's a little bit of concern that you can detect that the currency can't quite break through some of the levels we're at," Webber said. "That may be weighing on sentiment just a little."
Analysts said U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on July 22 would be the next large hurdle for the Canadian bond market.
"We're stuck in a range until the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week," said Rob Palombi, senior fixed-income analyst with MMS International.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.10 to C$109.06 to yield 6.018 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.26 percent.
The negative spread between the two benchmark bonds was 24 basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.22 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.20 percent.
